title: Eddie Jackson's sousaphone and huge tone
summary: They recall Eddie Jackson, who played sousaphone in brass bands and had a tone heard blocks away.

story.theme_name: Trombonists: who they heard, admired and learned from
story.community_name: Talking trombonists: who played the slide and how

blocks.x: I know he didn't play. I know he played a lot of tuba.
Yeah, he had, no, he had, uh, he had put his, the tube up and he played bass with the, the, the, the Nola band. Oh, yeah? With Pila Kass.
I didn't like that. I didn't know that. Yeah, I played a job with him. I know he played a lot of tuba already.
Yeah, I played a lot of job with him with his bass plowing. He used to read pretty nicely. Yeah? What kind of tuba would he have?
I don't know if it was a, he found a double P, but I know, uh, I know he used to make it ring up.
Was it a, oh, come up over?
A sousaphone. A sousaphone. A sousaphone.
Yeah, but Eddie used to have upright. Yeah? I don't remember upright.
I mean, every time I saw him, he had a sousaphone.

I remember Eddie used to make all that noise when they blow their, pick it up, them fences there, man. Pass by old feather aids there and blow there and knock the fence down. Pass by who? Old feather aids, the old fences, you know? Oh, no.
Picket fence, you know, the vibration to knock it loose.
Knock the whole plank out of the fence.
I think he got more tone on a bass tuba than just about anybody in this section. He had a tone. He was getting anything with it.
Yeah, but he didn't know.
I mean, I don't care how big the brass band, you wouldn't have to wonder who was playing tuba. You knew.
You're really hearing, huh?
Yeah, man. Blocks away.
Anybody around the place as well as he does now in Cuba, you think?
Place as well?
Yeah.
Anything like him? Around town?
